acceptedAnswer.text: Implant surgery is done under sedation. You feel nothing during it, and most patients have no memory of the appointment at all. Afterwards, patients generally report minor discomfort managed with over-the-counter medication.
Rest for a few days. Most people are back to normal activity within a week. A soft-food diet is needed for the next several months while the implants integrate with the jawbone.

Many patients already are. Others qualify after preparatory treatment such as bone grafting or extractions. It is not something to guess at. Candidacy is determined properly from a comprehensive consultation and a 3D scan.

They are designed to last decades, and can last the rest of your life. Surgical precision, materials and your own habits are what decide it. Implants have held a published success rate above 95% since they were introduced.

Yes. Implant restorations resist decay, but the gum around an implant can still develop peri-implantitis from plaque and tartar. Brush twice daily, floss once, and keep the six-month hygiene appointments.

mainEntity.name: Will I leave surgery without teeth?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. In most cases you leave the same visit wearing a fixed PMMA provisional prosthesis, which stays in place while the implants integrate.
Yes: upper, lower, or both. Cases are described here as single arch or double arch for exactly that reason.

mainEntity.name: What if I have bone loss?

acceptedAnswer.text: All-on-4 is often the answer because of bone loss: the rear implants are angled to reach denser bone. Some cases still need grafting first, which the cone-beam scan determines at the consultation.
Nitrous oxide, oral sedation and IV sedation. Oral and IV are administered by a medical anaesthesiologist and need transport arranged both ways.

mainEntity.name: How long until it is finished?

acceptedAnswer.text: Three to four months from surgery to the final zirconia prosthesis, then a further two to four months for complete healing around it.

mainEntity.name: Why is there no price list on this page?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because an honest one cannot exist. Two people missing the same tooth can need entirely different treatment depending on how long it has been gone and what the bone is doing. You get a real number after the scan, in writing, at the consultation.

Some plans offer limited coverage. The practice files claims on your behalf and works to get every benefit your plan entitles you to. Whether that is a large or small share depends entirely on the plan.

mainEntity.name: Can I finance the whole case?

acceptedAnswer.text: In most cases yes, through CareCredit, Proceed Finance or LendingClub. Proceed Finance in particular is designed for patients whose credit score would rule out conventional lending, with terms up to 96 months.

mainEntity.name: Is a second opinion really free?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, on implant surgery. If you have been quoted elsewhere, bring the plan and any imaging.
